summary: Edwin Abbott Abbott studied at the City of London School and St John's College (1857–1861). He held posts at St John's College (1861–1863), King Edward's School, Birmingham, Clifton College, and City of London School (1865–1889).

Edwin Arnold was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Japanology. He studied at King's College London and University College, Oxford. He served as principal of Deccan College (1856–1861) and held posts at King Edward's School, Mumbai, and Keio University.

Edwin Capers Kirkland worked in Indology and other fields. He earned his Ph.D. at Northwestern University, taught at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (circa 1934–1946), and was appointed Professor of English at the University of Florida in 1946.

Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Trinity College Dublin (circa 1857–1861), he served as President of The Asiatic Society (1886–1887) and Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (circa 1888–1890).

Edwin Francis Bryant is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his doctorate at Columbia University (circa 1991–1997). He taught at Harvard University (circa 1998–2002) and became Associate Professor of Hinduism at Rutgers University circa 2003.

Indology and philosophy scholar Edwin Gerow earned his PhD from the University of Chicago, studying under Louis Renou and others. His career included posts at Columbia, Rochester, Washington, the University of Chicago (1973), and Reed College (1989–1997).

Edwin Greaves, a scholar in Indology and linguistics, studied at Western College (circa 1877–1881). He served with the London Missionary Society (circa 1881–1920) and was principal of its college in Benares and the Missionary Language School in Lucknow.

Edwin Hotchkiss Tuttle was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Yale University (circa 1897–1901). He worked as a language teacher at Mackenzie School (circa 1902–1904) and Boys' Latin School of Maryland (circa 1904–1906).

Edwin Lee Johnson was a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Mississippi and Vanderbilt University (Ph.D. 1910). He taught at Quitman College, Alexander Institute, and Vanderbilt, becoming Professor of Latin and Greek there in 1935.
Indology scholar Edwin Möhrke studied philology at the University of Marburg in 1923 and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Königsberg under Helmuth von Glasenapp by 1934.

Edwin Norris worked in linguistics, Indology, and history and archaeology. He held posts at the East India Company (1818–1837), Royal Asiatic Society (1837–1861), the Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society, and the Foreign Office (1847–1866).

Edwin Whitfield Fay, a linguistics and Indology scholar, earned his Ph.D. at Johns Hopkins and studied at Leipzig. He held posts at the University of Michigan, Washington and Lee University, and the University of Texas at Austin.

Egaku Maeda specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a doctorate at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, Shoson Miyamoto, Hajime Nakamura, and Kogen Mizuno. He held professorships at Tokai Gakuen, Meijo, and Aichi Gakuin University (1972–2002).

Egon Wellesz studied at the University of Vienna from circa 1905 to 1908. He later held an academic post at the University of Vienna (circa 1913–1938) and served as a lecturer at the University of Oxford in 1943.

Eido Shimano, a Buddhist and religious studies figure, studied under Kengan Goto, Keizan Shirozou, and Soen Nakagawa, attending Ryutaku-ji and the University of Hawaiʻi. He led the Zen Studies Society, New York Zendo Shobo-ji, and Dai Bosatsu Zendo Kongo-ji.

Eiichi Imoto, a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indology fields, studied at Kyoto University from circa 1950 to 1958. He held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (circa 1964–1993) and Momoyama Gakuin University (circa 1993–2000).

Eiichi Makino, a scholar of philosophy and other fields, studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1899–1903). He held a post there from circa 1903 to 1938, as well as positions at Kyushu, Tohoku, and Chuo universities.
Eiichi Otani is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Toyo University (circa 1987–1991). He served as professor and dean at Kyoto Bunkyo University circa 2005.

Eiichi Yamaguchi is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed graduate studies at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1990). He served as a research assistant at Kyushu University (attested 1990–1991) and as a lecturer at Ariake College (attested 1997).
Eiju Fukushima works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and religious studies. Fukushima is attested in 2026 as a faculty member at both Otani University and the Otani Academic Society.
